# Loading, empty and errors

A page is never blank and never silent. While it loads, it shows its shape; when it has nothing, it says why and what comes next; when something fails, it says what and offers a way on.

On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/patterns/states

The previews are the site's illustrations, in HTML, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `muted`), which are
not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX.

## Loading

- The page header shows at once: its title is known from the address. Only the content waits.
- Nothing in the first 300 milliseconds, then a skeleton (`jl-skeleton`) shaped like what is coming: rows for a list, cards for a grid, lines for a text.
- A refresh keeps the content on screen until the new one arrives: no skeletons at every live update.
- An action shows that it runs on its own button (`loading`); a long one shows its steps. See [Feedback](feedback.md).

`jl-load-state` does all of it: wrap the content in it and call `load({ fetch, draw, isEmpty })`. It waits, shows the skeleton, then the content, the empty state of its `empty` slot, or the error with **Try again**; a later `load()` keeps the content while it refreshes.

```ts
const list = this._refs.state; // a <jl-load-state> around the rows, with a <jl-empty slot="empty">
await list.load({
  fetch: () => api.orders.list(filters),
  draw: (orders) => this.drawRows(orders),
  isEmpty: (orders) => orders.length === 0,
});
```

**Do**: The shape of what is coming: the page does not jump when it arrives.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <div class="row">
    <jl-skeleton shape="circle" width="32px" height="32px"></jl-skeleton>
    <div class="stack">
      <jl-skeleton width="60%"></jl-skeleton>
      <jl-skeleton width="35%"></jl-skeleton>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">
    <jl-skeleton shape="circle" width="32px" height="32px"></jl-skeleton>
    <div class="stack">
      <jl-skeleton width="60%"></jl-skeleton>
      <jl-skeleton width="35%"></jl-skeleton>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="row">
    <jl-skeleton shape="circle" width="32px" height="32px"></jl-skeleton>
    <div class="stack">
      <jl-skeleton width="60%"></jl-skeleton>
      <jl-skeleton width="35%"></jl-skeleton>
    </div>
  </div></div>
```

**Don't**: A spinner in an empty page says that something happens, not what.

```html
<jl-spinner size="32" label="Loading"></jl-spinner>
```

## From page to page

- The page shown stays, usable, until the next one has its data; then the next one takes its place in one go, never half drawn.
- Meanwhile a thin line over the top of the page says the next one is on its way: nothing in the first 150 milliseconds, then growing, fast then slower, never at the end; it runs to the end when the page comes.
- A page whose data takes more than 3 seconds shows anyway, its skeletons in place: people see that it came.
- The first page of a visit shows at once, with its skeletons: there is nothing to keep.

`jl-page-outlet` does it: the router shows its pages through it, and each page loads its data in its `jl-load-state`s as it would anyway. For another wait that replaces what is shown, a `jl-loading-bar` alone.

```ts
const outlet = document.querySelector('jl-page-outlet'); // where the pages go, in the app shell's main area
router.mountOn(outlet, { show: (page) => outlet.show(page) });
```

## Empty states

An empty collection shows a `jl-empty`: an icon, a heading, a sentence, and an action when there is one to take. Three cases, three kinds of words:

| Case | It says | For example |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing yet | What will be here, and how it gets here; the action that makes the first one, when the person may. | "No articles yet. Articles are what employees order from the shop." **New article** |
| Nothing matches | What found nothing, and the way back. | "No article matches “cable”. Try another word or another category." **Clear the search** |
| All done | That the work is done, calmly. | "You are all caught up. New reviews show up here as workflows send them." |

**Do**: What would be here, and the way to the first one.

```html
<jl-empty icon="package" heading="No articles yet" description="Articles are what employees order from the shop."><jl-button variant="primary" icon="plus" label="New article"></jl-button></jl-empty>
```

**Don't**: A bare line says neither what would be here nor how to get it.

```html
<span class="muted">None set up yet.</span>
```

- Inside a card or a narrow panel, `size="sm"`.
- Never "Nothing here" for an empty list: that is what a missing page says.

## Errors

An error shows where its cause is, says what happened in plain words, and offers the way on. See [Writing](https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/design/writing) for the words.

| What failed | Shown | With |
|---|---|---|
| An answer in a form | Under its field | How to put it right. |
| Saving a form or a dialog | In a `jl-alert` at the top of the form, or above the dialog's buttons | What the server said; the fields keep their values. |
| An action from a row, a switch, a menu | In a danger toast | What failed and why; a change shown in advance goes back. |
| Loading a page or a list | In place of the content: the error of `jl-load-state` | "The orders could not be loaded", and **Try again**. |
| A thing that does not exist | In place of the page | "This order does not exist", and a link to the list. |
| A page of another role | In place of the page | "For administrators", and who to ask. |
| The server out of reach | In a bar at the top of the main area, until it is back | "No connection: changes are not saved until it comes back." It tries again by itself. |

**Do**: In place of what is missing, with what to do.

```html
<jl-empty icon="circle-alert" heading="The orders could not be loaded" description="The server did not answer. Nothing was changed."><jl-button icon="refresh" label="Try again"></jl-button></jl-empty>
```

**Don't**: A toast over an empty page: it goes, the page stays blank, and "500" means nothing to the reader.

```html
<jl-toast tone="danger" heading="The server answered 500."></jl-toast>
```

## Not found, not allowed

- An unknown address: "This page does not exist", and a link home.
- A thing that is gone: "This order does not exist. It may have been deleted, or the link is wrong.", and a link to its list.
- A page of another role: "For administrators. Ask an administrator of your company to …".
- Each is a state of the page, where people can read it, not a toast followed by a jump to another page.

## Sessions and connections

- A session that ends leads to the sign-in page with the reason, "Your session ended. Sign in again to carry on.", then back to the page people were on.
- Work in progress is kept: an editor saves its draft on the device before leaving.
- When the server is out of reach, one bar says so, not a toast for each request that failed.
